# Cash game night or tournament night?

*The two ways to run a poker night, side by side — and how to pick the right one for your group.*

2 min read · Updated 2026-09-26

Both formats use the same rules and the same hands. The difference is what the chips mean and how the night ends.

## Side by side

| What changes | Cash game | Tournament |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chips | Each buy-in is a fixed number of chips; results are counted in chips at the end | Tournament chips only decide who survives; everyone starts equal |
| Blinds | Stay the same all night | Go up on a clock |
| Joining and leaving | Come and go any time | Everyone starts together; you leave when you run out of chips |
| Rebuys | Whenever you’re short | Only in an early rebuy period, if at all |
| How it ends | At an agreed time | When one player has every chip |
| Result | Everyone’s net: chips at the end minus buy-ins | A finishing order: 1st, 2nd, 3rd… |
| Pace | Relaxed, social | Builds to a final-table climax |

## Choose a cash game if…

- People arrive and leave at different times.
- You want a relaxed, chatty evening.
- Some players are beginners — nobody sits out after busting early; they just rebuy or leave when they like.
- You want Poker Night to track everything: buy-ins, rebuys, chips at the end and who pays whom.

## Choose a tournament if…

- Everyone can start at the same time.
- Your group likes a clear winner and a bit of drama.
- You want the night to have a natural end.
- You have a timer and a blind structure ready — see the structure templates.

> **Tip — Plan for early busts:** Players knocked out in the first hour get bored. Offer a rebuy period for the first few levels, or start a side cash game for anyone who’s out.

## Tournament basics

- **Freezeout:** one entry each, no rebuys. Simplest to run.
- **Rebuy / re-entry:** busted players can buy back in with a fresh stack until the end of an agreed level, usually the first break.
- **Add-on:** at the first break, everyone may take one extra stack, often smaller than the starting stack.
- **Places:** agree up front how the buy-ins are divided by finishing place. A common split for 6–9 players is 65 / 35 for the top two; for 10 or more, 50 / 30 / 20 for the top three.
